# Example transcript: running s01 on a sample file.
#
# This is an ILLUSTRATIVE run, not a byte-exact fixture — the LLM reply is
# non-deterministic, so what matters is the SHAPE: one round-trip, then one
# "Applied edit to ..." line. The tests in coder_test.go pin the deterministic
# parts (parsing, writing) with a fakeProvider; this file shows a learner what a
# real run looks like.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Set up a sample file to edit.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ cat > /tmp/hello.go <<'EOF'
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	fmt.Println("hello")
}
EOF

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Run s01 with the verbose flag so we can see the request/response shape.
#    (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY must be set; or use -provider deepseek etc.)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
$ go run . -v /tmp/hello.go "add a doc comment above main"

# --- stderr (the -v trace) ---
[s01] provider=anthropic model=claude-sonnet-4-6 url=
[s01] sending 62 bytes of /tmp/hello.go + instruction "add a doc comment above main"
[s01] stop_reason=end_turn in=512 out=78 tokens

# --- stdout ---
Applied edit to /tmp/hello.go (96 bytes)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Inspect what the model wrote back. The whole file was rewritten; only the
#    requested change appears, everything else is preserved.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ cat /tmp/hello.go
package main

import "fmt"

// main is the program entry point and prints a greeting.
func main() {
	fmt.Println("hello")
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Try a different provider — nothing else changes (provider translation
#    happens at the boundary in provider_openai.go).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-...
$ go run . -provider deepseek /tmp/hello.go "rename the function comment to say 'entrypoint'"
Applied edit to /tmp/hello.go (94 bytes)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Failure shape: if the model replies without a fenced code block, s01
#    cannot parse an edit. It prints the raw reply and exits non-zero, leaving
#    the file untouched (no reflection in s01 — that arrives in s09).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run . /tmp/hello.go "this is fine, no changes needed"
[s01] could not parse an edit from the reply:
The file already looks correct; no changes are necessary.
coder error: no fenced code block found in reply
exit status 1

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. The deterministic tests (these DO run in CI, no network):
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go test ./...
ok  	learn-aider/s01	0.5s
